topic.title: Fans grade players like an appraisal
topic.claim: We judge Rohit and Kohli the way offices judge people: the last bad quarter erases the record.
topic.behaviour: Three ducks in one innings and the timeline wants them retired. Two days later India win the series and the mood changes without anyone admitting it was an overreaction.
topic.mechanism: Online anger is cheap and instant, and it gets rewarded with replies. The latest result is the only data point that feels real, so it counts for everything.
topic.group: Cricket fans and office workers, 24 to 32
topic.moment: You type 'should have retired' at 9 pm and quietly change your mind by Sunday.

turn.believed: We judge players on their whole career.
turn.actually: We judge them on the last match, the same way an appraisal judges you on the last quarter.

topic.villain: A feed that rewards the loudest reaction to the latest result
topic.because: Outrage gets engagement, and engagement is what the platforms and channels sell. Nobody earns anything from saying 'wait and see'.

proof.fact: India were 0/3 after the first over, with Rohit Sharma out on the first ball, Virat Kohli bowled for a four-ball duck and Shreyas Iyer out on the last ball. Fans said Rohit and Kohli should have retired three years ago, while many others still want the pair at the 2027 ODI World Cup.

topic.payoff: Test: would you give your own career the verdict you just gave Kohli on a bad day?
topic.send_to: The group-chat friend who declares a player finished after one bad innings.
real_details: India won the fifth ODI by 22 runs to take the series 3-1, two days after the collapse in the fourth
topic.news_peg: India's top-order ducks in the 4th ODI on 2026-11-13 and the series win on 2026-11-15
topic.why_now: The whole swing from outrage to relief happened inside two days.

score.why: We judge a player on the last match the way an appraisal judges us on the last quarter; the verdict test turns it on the reader.
